note: The three SCE consumer rounds of the November 9, 2026 release, used by the consumer tests whether or not they are scheduled in questions/season0.json.

rounds.question: What median expected one-year household spending growth will the New York Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations publish for October 2026 on November 9? Forecast the published household expectation, not realized spending growth.
rounds.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Survey of Consumer Expectations
rounds.methodology: National rotating panel of approximately 1,300 US household heads. HH Spending Change worksheet, Median point prediction column. The reference month labels responses, not the publication date.
rounds.cadence: monthly, official New York Fed economic-indicators calendar
rounds.resolve: First archived official SCE workbook captured from November 9 at 16:00 UTC through November 10 at 16:00 UTC containing the October 2026 median household spending growth. Match the exact worksheet, header and reference month; preserve that captured artifact and ignore subsequent revisions.

rounds.question: What mean probability that US stock prices will be higher one year ahead will the New York Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations publish for October 2026 on November 9? Forecast the survey's mean probability on a 0-100 scale, not the actual stock-market outcome.
rounds.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Survey of Consumer Expectations
rounds.methodology: National rotating panel of US household heads. Stock Prices worksheet; exact mean-probability column for higher US stock prices one year ahead. The mean subjective probability is a continuous survey aggregate.
rounds.cadence: monthly, official New York Fed economic-indicators calendar
rounds.resolve: First archived official SCE workbook captured from November 9 at 16:00 UTC through November 10 at 16:00 UTC containing October 2026 stock-price expectations. Read the exact mean probability of higher prices one year ahead; subsequent revisions do not replace the captured result.

rounds.question: What mean probability that the US unemployment rate will be higher one year ahead will the New York Fed Survey of Consumer Expectations publish for October 2026 on November 9? Forecast the survey's mean probability on a 0-100 scale, not the actual unemployment outcome.
rounds.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of New York, Survey of Consumer Expectations
rounds.methodology: National rotating panel of US household heads. Unemployment Expectations worksheet; exact mean-probability column for a higher US unemployment rate one year ahead. This is the population's expectation rather than realized unemployment.
rounds.cadence: monthly, official New York Fed economic-indicators calendar
rounds.resolve: First archived official SCE workbook captured from November 9 at 16:00 UTC through November 10 at 16:00 UTC containing October 2026 unemployment expectations. Match the exact mean probability and reference month; preserve the captured artifact against later revisions.
